SuperFlexSketch / DINO matching ablation

DINO without Hungarian matching.

We fine-tuned all weights of pretrained DINOv2 ViT-S/14, with a newly initialized 128-dimensional projection, SuperFlex transformer decoder, and heads predicting up to 16 deformable superquadrics. The sole experimental change was direct slot-to-slot teacher supervision instead of Hungarian assignment.

Both runs trained for 200 epochs, batch size 32, seed 42, using 17,988 sketches of 4,497 chairs. Adam with OneCycleLR used peak rates of 10⁻⁵ for the backbone and projection and 10⁻⁴ for the decoder and heads. Targets were canonical superquadrics from the pretrained point-cloud teacher. This experiment remains supervised.

How closely does the network reproduce its GT superquadrics?

Primary metric: IoU against the teacher superquadric union. This isolates agreement with the training target. Original-mesh IoU below measures reconstruction fidelity including limitations of the teacher representation.

Original-mesh finding: removing matching costs 0.14 IoU percentage points (0.48% relative) at epoch 200, with only 0.7% less wall time. This one-seed result supports simplification with a small observed accuracy cost; it does not establish statistical equivalence.

Training, checkpoint selection & interpretation
  • The complete DINO backbone is trainable from the start. Projection, decoder and primitive heads start fresh; no previous sketch checkpoint is resumed. Inputs are 224 × 224 RGB-replicated sketches with ImageNet normalization, without augmentation. Adam uses no weight decay.
  • The loss combines primitive surface Chamfer, auxiliary geometry, and existence BCE with weights 1, 1, and 0.04. Identity matching pairs predicted slot i directly with teacher slot i. Canonical coordinates align shapes but do not guarantee consistent primitive slots. Whole-shape occupancy IoU provides the common comparison metric.
  • For visual comparison, each model uses its saved peak-validation-IoU checkpoint: Hungarian epoch 170, identity epoch 190. The table also compares both models at epoch 200. Identity’s loss-selected best.pt is epoch 60 (IoU 0.229077), so it is not used here. These are validation-selected results, not an independent test set.
  • Selection is unchanged: eight view-00 validation objects sampled with NumPy seed 42, then twelve from the remaining objects with seed 43. There is no selection by prediction quality.
  • GT superquadrics are exact teacher labels from data/sketch_primitive/gt/val.npz. Compare original mesh → GT SQ to inspect target limitations, then GT SQ → predictions to inspect network errors. Both IoU metrics use the same 4,096 deterministic canonical query points. Primary IoU compares predicted occupancy with GT-SQ occupancy; secondary IoU compares with original-mesh voxel occupancy. GT-SQ self-IoU is 1 by definition. Queries cover the original mesh bounding box plus 10% margin, so these are finite-domain sampled estimates. The teacher is a reference, not a guaranteed ceiling.
  • Only existence > 0.5 primitives are rendered, including tapering and bending. Colors identify parts within a reconstruction, not matched or semantic parts across columns. Four camera directions are synchronized; each mesh is framed independently, so images are not pixel-aligned overlays.

Sketch → original mesh → GT superquadrics → DINO with Hungarian → DINO without matching.
Δ is no-matching minus Hungarian IoU against GT superquadrics for the displayed checkpoints.
